Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import os,re,json
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))

def comps(g):
    n=len(g); cs=[]; seen=set()
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            if g[i][j] and (i,j) not in seen:
                c=g[i][j]; st=[(i,j)]; cl=[]; seen.add((i,j))
                while st:
                    y,x=st.pop(); cl.append((y,x))
                    for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                        ny,nx=y+dy,x+dx
                        if 0<=ny<n and 0<=nx<n and g[ny][nx]==c and (ny,nx) not in seen:
                            seen.add((ny,nx)); st.append((ny,nx))
                cs.append((c,cl))
    return cs

def solve(I):
    n=len(I); cs=[]; seen=set()
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            if I[i][j] and (i,j) not in seen:
                c=I[i][j]; st=[(i,j)]; cl=[]; seen.add((i,j))
                while st:
                    y,x=st.pop(); cl.append((y,x))
                    for dy,dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                        ny,nx=y+dy,x+dx
                        if 0<=ny<n and 0<=nx<n and I[ny][nx]==c and (ny,nx) not in seen:
                            seen.add((ny,nx)); st.append((ny,nx))
                cs.append((c,tuple(sorted(cl))))
    order=sorted(cs,key=lambda o:(min(p[0] for p in o[1])+min(p[1] for p in o[1]), min(p[0] for p in o[1]),min(p[1] for p in o[1])))
    R=[[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
    occupied=set()
    for idx,(c,cells) in enumerate(order):
        h=max(p[0] for p in cells)-min(p[0] for p in cells)+1
        w=max(p[1] for p in cells)-min(p[1] for p in cells)+1
        tl=min(cells)
        shape={(y-tl[0], x-tl[1]) for y,x in cells}
        anch=(max(y for y,_ in occupied), max(x for _,x in occupied)) if occupied else None
        best=None
        # candidate: TL at (anch+? ) anchor is prev BR; we want obj cell covering that BR point
        opts=[]
        if anch is None:
            ty,tx=0,0; opts=[(0,0,{(ty+y,tx+x) for y,x in shape})]
        else:
            # TL must equal anch if shape allows, else minimal displacement so SOME cell == anch OR adjacent-free
            for dy in range(-h+1,h+2):
                for dx in range(-w+1,w+2):
                    ty,tx=anch[0]+dy,anch[1]+dx
                    ct={(ty+y,tx+x) for y,x in shape}
                    if any(y<0 or x<0 or y>=n or x>=n for y,x in ct): continue
                    if ct & occupied: continue
                    opts.append((abs(dy)+abs(dx), abs(dy), abs(dx), ty, tx, ct))
        opts.sort(key=lambda t:t[:3])
        if not opts: continue
        _,_,_,ty,tx,ct=opts[0]
        for y,x in ct: R[y][x]=c
        occupied.update(ct)
    return R
